{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfhkk7676h94t71NyXpdG","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01HsNDKKMSkpGnnss2vYCzRW","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"cd floydwarshall && cat > /tmp/kernels.txt <<'EOF'\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Hybrid MPI + OpenMP + CUDA blocked Floyd-Warshall\n//\n// Data layout: row-major dist[i][j] == dist[idx2(j, i, n)], identical to the\n// original code. Rows are distributed across MPI ranks in contiguous groups\n// of BK-row blocks; each rank owns one GPU. Columns are padded to a multiple\n// of TC with a large \"unreachable\" value so that padded nodes never improve\n// any real path.\n//\n// For every k-block (BK intermediate nodes) the owning rank finalizes the\n// pivot row panel (phase 1 + phase 2 row), broadcasts it to all ranks, and\n// every rank then updates its own rows (phase 2 column + phase 3). The next\n// pivot panel is computed on a high-priority stream and broadcast while the\n// bulk phase-3 update of the current k-block is still running (lookahead).\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nconstexpr int BK = 32;                  // k-block size / row-block size\nconstexpr int TC = 128;                 // phase-3 tile width (columns)\nconstexpr unsigned int PADV = 1u << 20; // distance used for padding entries\nconstexpr int PSHIFT = 6;               // packing: (dist << 6) | (kk + 1)\n\n#define CUDA_CHECK(call)                                                        \\\n    do {                                                                        \\\n        cudaError_t err_ = (call);                                              \\\n        if (err_ != cudaSuccess) {                                              \\\n            fprintf(stderr, \"CUDA error %s at %s:%d\\n\", cudaGetErrorString(err_), \\\n                    __FILE__, __LINE__);                                        \\\n            MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);                                       \\\n        }                                                                       \\\n    } while (0)\n\n// Phase 1: diagonal tile (rows/cols k0..k0+BK) relaxed in place.\n// Row kk and column kk never change during step kk (diagonal is zero), so a\n// single barrier per step suffices.\n__global__ void __launch_bounds__(BK * BK)\nfwPhase1(unsigned int* __restrict__ d, unsigned int* __restrict__ p, size_t ld,\n         int lr0, int k0) {\n    __shared__ unsigned int t[BK][BK + 1];\n    const int tx = threadIdx.x, ty = threadIdx.y;\n    const size_t g = (size_t)(lr0 + ty) * ld + k0 + tx;\n    unsigned int v = d[g];\n    unsigned int pv = 0;\n    bool changed = false;\n    t[ty][tx] = v;\n    __syncthreads();\n#pragma unroll 8\n    for (int kk = 0; kk < BK; ++kk) {\n        const unsigned int nd = t[ty][kk] + t[kk][tx];\n        if (nd < v) {\n            v = nd;\n            pv = k0 + kk;\n            changed = true;\n            t[ty][tx] = v;\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n    }\n    if (changed) {\n        d[g] = v;\n        p[g] = pv;\n    }\n}\n\n// Phase 2 (row): tiles of the pivot row panel, using the finished diagonal tile.\n__global__ void __launch_bounds__(BK * BK)\nfwPhase2Row(unsigned int* __restrict__ d, unsigned int* __restrict__ p, size_t ld,\n            int lr0, int k0) {\n    const int jb = blockIdx.x;\n    if (jb * BK == k0) return;\n    __shared__ unsigned int sd[BK][BK + 1];\n    __shared__ unsigned int t[BK][BK + 1];\n    const int tx = threadIdx.x, ty = threadIdx.y;\n    const size_t rowOff = (size_t)(lr0 + ty) * ld;\n    const size_t g = rowOff + (size_t)jb * BK + tx;\n    sd[ty][tx] = d[rowOff + k0 + tx];\n    unsigned int v = d[g];\n    unsigned int pv = 0;\n    bool changed = false;\n    t[ty][tx] = v;\n    __syncthreads();\n#pragma unroll 8\n    for (int kk = 0; kk < BK; ++kk) {\n        const unsigned int nd = sd[ty][kk] + t[kk][tx];\n        if (nd < v) {\n            v = nd;\n            pv = k0 + kk;\n            changed = true;\n            t[ty][tx] = v;\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n    }\n    if (changed) {\n        d[g] = v;\n        p[g] = pv;\n    }\n}\n\n// Phase 2 (column): tile (row block, pivot columns) of every local row block,\n// using the diagonal tile from the pivot panel. {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfhmZL5kRUmoudfVsMhh8","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01RCKsNamBN5AxJuY33XQuyA","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"cd /tmp && cat > bc2.cpp <<'EOF'\n#include <mpi.h>\n#include <cuda_runtime.h>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <vector>\n#include <chrono>\nint r,s;\nvoid flat(unsigned*b,int cnt,int root){ if(r==root){std::vector<MPI_Request> q; for(int p=0;p<s;++p) if(p!=root){q.emplace_back(); MPI_Isend(b,cnt,MPI_UNSIGNED,p,7,MPI_COMM_WORLD,&q.back());} MPI_Waitall(q.size(),q.data(),MPI_STATUSES_IGNORE);} else MPI_Recv(b,cnt,MPI_UNSIGNED,root,7,MPI_COMM_WORLD,MPI_STATUS_IGNORE);}\n// pipelined chain: root -> root+1 -> ... in chunks\nvoid chain(unsigned*b,int cnt,int root,int nch){ int vr=(r-root+s)%s; int prev=(r-1+s)%s, next=(r+1)%s; int cs=(cnt+nch-1)/nch; std::vector<MPI_Request> q;\n for(int c=0;c<nch;++c){int o=c*cs, n=std::min(cs,cnt-o); if(n<=0)break; if(vr>0) MPI_Recv(b+o,n,MPI_UNSIGNED,prev,8,MPI_COMM_WORLD,MPI_STATUS_IGNORE); {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfhq1P2C4KtnB5wzESxrY","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I've rewritten `floydwarshall/floydwarshall.cpp` as a hybrid MPI + OpenMP + CUDA program. It always runs that way, and the executable name is still `floydwarshall`. The distance matrix matches the original's hash exactly on every test, and the 4-GPU run is about 3.7× faster than 1 GPU at the largest size.\n\n**Results on this machine (4× RTX 3090, Open MPI 4.1.6)**\n\n| n | 1 GPU | 2 GPUs | 4 GPUs |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 512 (default) | 2 ms (original serial: 165 ms) | | |\n| 2048 | 6 ms (original serial: 9375 ms) | | |\n| 8192 | 174 ms | 97 ms | 56 ms |\n| 16384 | 1295 ms | 763 ms | 340 ms (about 12.9 TOPS) |\n| 32768 | 11.2 s | 6.8 s | 2.9 s |\n\n**Correctness checks:** I compared the distance-matrix hash with the original build for n = 0, 1, 2, 31, 33, 100, 129, 512, 1000, 2048 and 3001, using 1–6 ranks. Every case matched and `-v` passed. I also checked the multi-node and fallback communication paths by faking node boundaries on this single machine; they also matched. I haven't run on a real multi-node cluster.\n\n**How it's split up:**\n- **MPI:** each rank owns a contiguous band of rows and one GPU, chosen by its rank within the node.\n- **CUDA:** the algorithm runs in 32×32 blocks. The rank that owns the current block of rows finishes it and sends it to all other ranks; every rank then updates its own rows. The next block is computed and sent on a high-priority stream while the current update is still running, so communication overlaps computation.\n- **OpenMP:** rank 0's host work, i.e. packing/unpacking the matrices, the max-weight scan and validation.\n\n**Things that behave differently from what you might assume:**\n- **Transfers are compressed losslessly.** The graph is complete, so no shortest distance can exceed the largest edge weight (about 201 here). Data is therefore sent as 1-byte values, chosen at runtime (2 or 4 bytes if weights are larger). This cut communication 4×.\n- **MPI is bypassed between ranks on the same node.** `MPI_Bcast` here only reached about 1.7 GB/s and was the bottleneck. Ranks on the same node now exchange data through MPI shared-memory windows instead. Between nodes, `MPI_Bcast` is still used. If nodes run different numbers of ranks, it falls back to plain `MPI_Bcast`.\n- **Shared memory is needed on rank 0's node.** The full matrix is staged there, so for n=32768 about 2 GB of `/dev/shm` is used. That's fine here (504 GB free), but small `/dev/shm` limits like container defaults would break large runs.\n- **The timing covers more than the original's.** It includes sending the input to the GPUs, the computation, and collecting the distance matrix on rank 0.\n- **The `path` matrix is still computed and collected on rank 0, but after the timer stops.** The original never outputs it.\n- **`path` can differ from the original's.** Distances are identical, but the blocked order can record a different intermediate node when several shortest paths are tied. I checked that every entry still points to a valid shortest path.\n- **There is a hard limit on edge weights.** The fast kernel assumes they stay below 2^19, and the program stops with an error if they don't. The benchmark's maximum is 201.\n\n**`CMakeLists.txt` changes:** the source file is compiled as CUDA for the GPU on the build machine (`native`), and the build links MPI, OpenMP and the CUDA runtime. It now requires CMake 3.24 or newer.\n\nRun it with, for example, `mpirun -np 4 ./floydwarshall -n 16384`, one rank per GPU."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":511,"cache_read_input_tokens":145152,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":511},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"98dcefb4-01cd-4e4f-854d-81d2559bdc25","uuid":"d60f9d7d-b777-4f1c-bb89-b343070b600a","timestamp":"2026-10-04T20:28:57.614Z","request_id":"req_011Cfhq1Ne7jJP6uHJ1ACS8V"}
